content.text:
I've migrated all four modules in `src/services/` to the repository pattern, but the API routes are now broken. Every route in `src/api/routes.js` still calls a service function with a callback, and those functions now return promises instead. The callback never runs, so all five endpoints hang. The dispatcher only flagged one of them (line 12).

I re-ran the full test suite myself: 10 pass, 0 fail. No test covers `routes.js`, which is why the break didn't show up. Nothing is committed.

| Module | Repository used | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `user-service.js` | `UserRepository` (already existed) | Straight mapping to `findActive`, `findById` and `softDelete`. |
| `order-service.js` | `OrderRepository` (already existed) | Uses `findByUser` and `findPaid`. |
| `payment-service.js` | **New** `PaymentRepository` | No payment repository existed, so the worker created `src/repositories/payment-repository.js`, built like the other two. The dispatcher had told workers to report a blocker in this case instead, so check it's what you want. |
| `auth-service.js` | `UserRepository` | It has no find-by-email method, so `findByEmail` loads every active user and filters by email. That's fine for the in-memory database here but slow on a real one. Adding a repository method would fix it. |

All four test files in `tests/` were converted to async/await. The workers' notes are in `.agent-work/migration/`, which is untracked; delete it or add it to `.gitignore` before committing.

**Decision for you:** the fix is to have each route handler wait for the promise and pass the result or error to its callback, e.g. `totalPaidCents().then((r) => cb(null, r), cb)`. Want me to make that change?

I've migrated all four modules in `src/services/` to the repository pattern, but the API routes are now broken. Every route in `src/api/routes.js` still calls a service function with a callback, and those functions now return promises instead. The callback never runs, so all five endpoints hang. The dispatcher only flagged one of them (line 12).

I re-ran the full test suite myself: 10 pass, 0 fail. No test covers `routes.js`, which is why the break didn't show up. Nothing is committed.

| Module | Repository used | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `user-service.js` | `UserRepository` (already existed) | Straight mapping to `findActive`, `findById` and `softDelete`. |
| `order-service.js` | `OrderRepository` (already existed) | Uses `findByUser` and `findPaid`. |
| `payment-service.js` | **New** `PaymentRepository` | No payment repository existed, so the worker created `src/repositories/payment-repository.js`, built like the other two. The dispatcher had told workers to report a blocker in this case instead, so check it's what you want. |
| `auth-service.js` | `UserRepository` | It has no find-by-email method, so `findByEmail` loads every active user and filters by email. That's fine for the in-memory database here but slow on a real one. Adding a repository method would fix it. |

All four test files in `tests/` were converted to async/await. The workers' notes are in `.agent-work/migration/`, which is untracked; delete it or add it to `.gitignore` before committing.

**Decision for you:** the fix is to have each route handler wait for the promise and pass the result or error to its callback, e.g. `totalPaidCents().then((r) => cb(null, r), cb)`. Want me to make that change?
